meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and was anyone going to call me first?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. And Owen found out on his phone, in the middle of a class. What was the zero based on, Hale?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing down November 2. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot about one phrase and one paragraph is a conversation, not a document. Show me what you wrote that day.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
I'm writing down October 15. Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's called drafting. Put the outline and the essay side by side in front of me.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing today, not Friday at 3. The zero comes out of the gradebook tonight, and the outline and the essay are still not in front of me. Is the rewrite private, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You apologised for entering the zero before calling me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook, the rewrite kept private, and the October 15 outline and the essay put in front of me. I expect all of that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback, because you cited 4.4 and committed to the rewrite, but she had not reached her last position and still wants the zero out of the gradebook, the offer in writing today, the outline and essay side by side, and the rewrite kept private; once those are in place that is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one sentence and then gave dated specifics, and your commitment to a rewrite with nothing on his record met her fallback demand.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite before showing the outline and the essay together, so your evidence stayed something you said rather than something she could check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed on the October 15 outline and the November 2 conversation, so it never came near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Put the outline and the essay in front of her before you mention the rewrite, so the offer rests on something she has checked.
